key_insight: Superfluid helium-4 near a solid wall still follows a logarithmic law of the wall, but with a strongly reduced, nearly temperature-invariant effective Kármán constant that signals nonclassical near-wall dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical scaling rule for predicting wall shear and flow behavior in He II transport, which is important for cryogenic cooling system design and operation.
method: Molecular tagging velocimetry to visualize near-wall velocity fields in mechanically driven He II pipe flow
Pressure-drop measurements to independently infer wall shear stress
Tested flows up to Reynolds number 1.26×10^6 across a range of temperatures
evidence_signal: The abstract reports robust logarithmic velocity profiles in the normal-fluid component and an effective Kármán constant less than half the classical value, with little change across temperatures despite varying two-fluid fractions.
watch_item: The inferred wall law comes from specialized cryogenic pipe-flow experiments, so broader applicability to other geometries, heat loads, or flow regimes may require additional validation.
paper_title: A nonclassical law of the wall in superfluid helium-4
